title: The Next Generation of Analytical and Experimental Approaches for Collective Excitations with Monochromated Electron Energy-Loss Spectroscopy
content: Monochromated electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) is a technique ideally suited for studying collective excitations in nanomaterials due to the combined high spatial resolution and spectral resolution of the technique, along with a set of selection rules that are ideally suited for accessing these phenomena. As a result, the technique has been applied across many of the most critical quasiparticles that are active in the infrared regime (plasmons, polaritons, phonons, and excitons) for applications in biology, nanophotonics, quantum materials, and many more.
